exposure: Health insurance status (Health Insurance enrollees vs. Out-of-Pocket payers)
Mode of delivery (vaginal vs. caesarean section)
outcome: Cost of delivery (vaginal and caesarean section)
cohort: The study included 380 women (comprising 133 vaginal and 57 caesarean section deliveries among both Health Insurance enrollees and Out-of-Pocket payers) who accessed delivery services in a tertiary health institution in Southwest Nigeria.
finding: The total cost of both vaginal and caesarean section deliveries was found to be lower among Health Insurance enrollees compared to Out-of-Pocket payers.
mod_finding: For both vaginal and caesarean section deliveries, the mean total cost was significantly lower for Health Insurance enrollees than for Out-of-Pocket payers.
cross-section timing: At the time women accessed delivery services.
